subject.title: [Bug]: Kimi Coding auth fallback in systemd Gateway when config env is not injected

question: For managed Linux Gateway services, should config `env` provider keys be treated as a runtime-only config source, materialized into service environment files, or discouraged in favor of `.env`/auth profiles for daemon use?
rationale: The code already applies config env during config snapshot reads, but service install intentionally tracks keys without rendering raw config values, and status can inspect a different process env; choosing among those contracts affects credential persistence and user-facing diagnostics.

options.title: Keep Runtime Config Env
options.body: Keep config `env` as a runtime config source, add a Linux systemd/Kimi proof or regression test for the current path, and adjust status/docs only if that proof finds a remaining mismatch.

options.title: Materialize Service Env
options.body: Render supported config/env secrets into the systemd EnvironmentFile or a SecretRef-backed service source, accepting the new credential-persistence contract with explicit tests and docs.

options.title: Prefer Durable Auth Stores
options.body: Document daemon-provider keys as `.env` or per-agent auth-profile inputs and make `models status` warn when a config-only source may not represent a running managed service.

recommendation.title: Keep Runtime Config Env
recommendation.body: Keep config `env` as a runtime config source, add a Linux systemd/Kimi proof or regression test for the current path, and adjust status/docs only if that proof finds a remaining mismatch.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses config IO, service env planning, systemd rendering, and CLI status surfaces where steipete has the strongest history signal.
